title: Activepieces Docker Setup: 6 Mistakes to Avoid (2026)
summary: An activepieces Docker setup uses Docker Compose for three containers: app, Postgres, and Redis. You'll have all the integrations needed to self-host.
body_markdown:
## What Community Edition includes versus paid features


If you run it yourself, the Community Edition is free under the MIT licence. SSO beyond the Team plan, audit logs and embedding sit behind paid or sales-led arrangements.


### MIT-licensed Community Edition


In its own words, the MIT licence grants permission to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense and sell the software, "without restriction." It also says the software is provided "as is," without warranty of any kind.


For you, that means the code is yours to run and change, but nobody is contractually obliged to keep your instance up, patch it or answer when it fails.


### Paid plans and sales-led features


Read the infrastructure column first: it determines who is paged when something breaks. The table shows who holds the infrastructure and which capabilities change hands at each tier.


Licence Who runs infrastructure SSO Audit logs Embedding Support route


Community Edition self-hosted MIT You Not included Not included Not included Community channels


Cloud plans Commercial subscription Activepieces Beyond Team, by arrangement with sales Sales-led Sales-led Per plan, see the pricing page


Enterprise self-hosted Commercial agreement You, on your own infrastructure Included by agreement Included by agreement Included by agreement Contracted with sales


If you need SSO beyond the Team plan, audit logs or embedding, Community Edition isn't the route.


The sales form is the way to scope self-hosted enterprise, and what it scopes is not a cut-down build: the fully air-gapped edition carries the same access control, audit trail, release management and secret-manager hooks as the managed cloud, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


Don't write "SOC 2 compliant" in your own vendor review. SOC 2 is a programme Activepieces has in progress, not a certification it holds. Name the control you need, such as access logging or centralised authentication, and check the plan against that.


### When cloud beats self-hosting


When nobody on your team wants to own uptime, cloud is the better choice. If the vendor's cloud goes down, their team restores it; if your self-hosted instance goes down, you're the incident response, the backup restore and the certificate renewal.


Choose cloud for a small team, a first workflow or a pilot where an outage costs little and your time costs more than a subscription.


When data must stay on infrastructure you control, self-hosting wins.


Otherwise, build before committing: the free plan at[https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Factivepieces-docker-setup-6-mistakes-to-avoid-2026) costs $0 and gives you 1,000 credits a month, unlimited flows and up to 5 users, which means you can test before upgrading to a paid plan.


Compare plans at[https://www.activepieces.com/pricing](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) , and use[https://www.activepieces.com/sales](https://www.activepieces.com/sales) for self-hosted enterprise, SSO beyond Team, audit logs or embedding.
